title: Large Language Models’ Complicit Responses to Illicit Instructions across Socio-Legal Contexts
reasoning: The paper explicitly benchmarks LLMs based on religious identity, evaluating how model responses vary for different religious groups (e.g., Buddhist, Taoist, Muslim, Catholic, Christian) in illicit contexts. Furthermore, it employs a 'social-good perspective' to assess the ethical responsibility of models and uses 'morality' as a core dimension in its stereotype analysis of model reasoning traces.
